mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility, as seen in the last week, signals a broader return to out-of-home activities and commuting, which will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 2 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL time and increasing GROCERY_PHARM visits suggests a growing comfort with leaving home for essential and non-essential errands, which will spill over into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL time continues to decrease and GROCERY_PHARM visits continue to increase, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The relatively stable, albeit low, WORKPLACES mobility indicates that a baseline level of economic activity and weekday presence is maintained, preventing further RETAIL_REC declines and allowing for slight increases as other mobility factors improve over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains stable within +/- 1 point, but RETAIL_REC decreases significantly over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp increase in PARKS mobility in the most recent week indicates a strong public desire for outdoor activity and movement, which is a leading indicator for increased general out-of-home activity, including retail, over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and steady upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility reflects a sustained increase in essential out-of-home trips, building public confidence that will gradually extend to non-essential retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues its upward trend, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in TRANSIT mobility, even when WORKPLACES mobility remains stable, suggests an increase in non-work related travel (e.g., leisure, shopping), which directly contributes to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES remains within +/- 1 point
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises for two consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES mobility remains stable, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL time indicates a broader societal shift away from staying at home, creating more opportunities for all types of out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, which will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC also decreases over the next 14 days.
